correctness.rationale: The exponentials E(iu) form a Vandermonde basis and transport the quandle product to F(-u)G(2u). The derivation images of 1 and u are forced into the specified eigenpolynomial space; conversely first-order operators with those coefficients obey Leibniz, and the generators 1,u span the entire quandle algebra under star. Brackets follow ordinary first-order differential operator commutators. Direct original-basis linear nullity checks for p=3,5,7,11,17 and all monomial/basis bracket tests through p=31 corroborate the proof.

originality.rationale: The closest direct published derivation theorem (arxiv:2106.08289, Theorem 3.9) assumes characteristic zero; its Section 4.2 gives only small characteristic-p examples at quandle order up to 6, including the known p=3,5 special cases. Neither its results nor the 2026 integral odd-order automorphism results, even-order reduction, or Alexander augmentation analyses state the uniform matching-characteristic p-dimensional quandle derivation Lie algebra or full bracket. The same-object earlier idempotent-locus result solves different equations and does not imply derivation identities. Residual unindexed special-source risk remains.

value.rationale: Derivations form the natural Lie algebra of infinitesimal symmetries of a nonassociative algebra. The theorem determines that invariant uniformly across all odd prime dihedral quandles in the defining characteristic, exhibits arithmetic dependence on the multiplicative order of 2 (dimension 4 for p=17 and 6 for p=31), and determines the bracket and finite-field counts. These features are neither dictated by characteristic-zero rigidity nor inferable merely from the previously computed p=3,5 matrices.
